domain: Climate Policy / Political Economy / Intergenerational Ethics
topic_summary: Analysis of three competing readings of the climate-response kernel: mitigation-priority (decarbonize to prevent future harm), adaptation-priority (accept warming, invest in resilience), and degrowth (reduce material throughput to stay within planetary boundaries). Each reading instantiates a different constraint with distinct victim structures across generations and regions.

key_entities: Global North industrial economies (historical emitters, capital holders)
Global South developing economies (low historical emissions, high climate vulnerability)
Future generations (inheritors of climate system state, no current political voice)
Fossil fuel capital (stranded asset holders, transition resistors)
key_tensions: Intergenerational: current consumption vs future climate stability
North-South: historical responsibility vs current development rights
Growth-stability: GDP expansion vs planetary boundary constraints
key_mechanisms: Carbon pricing (mitigation tool, regressive without redistribution)
Adaptation finance (reactive investment in climate-resilient infrastructure)
Degrowth policy (consumption caps, work-time reduction, sufficiency norms)
key_absences: Geoengineering as fourth reading (solar radiation management, carbon removal)
Non-state actor enforcement (corporate voluntary commitments, investor pressure)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The shared commitment that humanity must respond to anthropogenic climate change, grounded in IPCC consensus on warming attribution and UNFCCC framework legitimacy
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Scientific consensus (IPCC) establishes the problem; UNFCCC/Paris framework provides procedural legitimacy; national sovereignty determines implementation

readings.commitment: Prevent future harm by rapid decarbonization; intergenerational justice requires minimizing warming
readings.authority_grounding: IPCC carbon budgets, Paris 1.5°C target, precautionary principle
readings.expected_structural_delta: Future generations primary beneficiaries; current generation bears transition costs; Global North bears disproportionate mitigation burden due to historical emissions; fossil capital enters victim set via stranded assets

readings.commitment: Accept 2-3°C warming as inevitable; invest in resilience rather than costly prevention
readings.authority_grounding: Cost-benefit analysis, technological optimism, revealed preference of continued emissions growth
readings.expected_structural_delta: Current generation primary beneficiary (avoids transition costs); future generations and Global South enter victim set (bear climate impacts without prevention); fossil capital protected; adaptation investment concentrates in wealthy regions

readings.commitment: Reduce material throughput to stay within planetary boundaries; sufficiency over efficiency
readings.authority_grounding: Ecological economics, planetary boundaries framework, critique of green growth feasibility
readings.expected_structural_delta: Planetary systems primary beneficiary (reduced extraction pressure); current Global North consumption patterns enter victim set (lifestyle reduction); Global South development constrained unless North reduces first; capital accumulation itself becomes extractive mechanism

axes.human_readable: Mitigation-Priority Reading (Prevent Future Harm via Decarbonization)
axes.structural_delta: Rapid emissions reduction to minimize warming; intergenerational justice via prevention
axes.primary_observable: Carbon budget compliance, renewable energy deployment rates, fossil fuel phase-out timelines
axes.selection_reason: First reading: establishes baseline intergenerational victim structure and mitigation constraint architecture

axes.human_readable: Adaptation-Priority Reading (Accept Warming, Invest in Resilience)
axes.structural_delta: Accept 2-3°C warming; prioritize adaptation investment over mitigation costs
axes.primary_observable: Adaptation finance flows, climate-resilient infrastructure investment, revealed emissions trajectories
axes.selection_reason: Second reading: inverts victim structure from mitigation reading; protects current consumption

axes.structural_delta: Material throughput reduction as primary response; sufficiency over technological efficiency
axes.primary_observable: GDP decoupling from emissions (absolute vs relative), work-time reduction policies, consumption cap proposals
axes.selection_reason: Third reading: challenges growth paradigm itself; distinct beneficiary/victim structure from both mitigation and adaptation

omegas.description: Geoengineering (solar radiation management, carbon dioxide removal) constitutes a potential fourth reading of the climate-response kernel, with distinct victim structure (governance risk, unilateral deployment, termination shock). Deferred due to three-reading budget and lower current policy salience.

All three readings embed contested assumptions about North-South equity (common but differentiated responsibilities, climate debt, development rights). The equity dimension is orthogonal to the mitigation/adaptation/degrowth axis but shapes extractiveness within each reading.

Mitigation reading assumes green growth feasibility (absolute decoupling of GDP from emissions); degrowth reading contests this. If decoupling is infeasible, mitigation collapses into degrowth. If feasible, degrowth is unnecessary. Empirical question with high structural stakes.

Intergenerational victim structure depends on discount rate choice (pure time preference vs declining marginal utility). Low discount rates favor mitigation; high rates favor adaptation. The discount rate itself is a contested normative parameter, not an observable.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure confirmed: three readings share the climate-response obligation substrate but instantiate genuinely different constraints with distinct beneficiary/victim structures and extractiveness profiles. North-South equity and discount rate choice are orthogonal dimensions documented as omegas.
